articles.title: JOIN AI LEADERS IN SONOMA FOR MONETIZE 2026: A PRIVATE STRIPE CONFERENCE
articles.summary:
The AI shift has upended traditional pricing: seat-based models are collapsing and token margins are unpredictable. Many product teams find themselves trapped between outdated billing systems and fast-evolving AI features.

Monetize [5] is a private summit crafted to give product leaders a practical perspective on the challenges they face with monetization in the AI era. From outcome-based pricing to agent-led growth, you'll learn what's actually working from leaders including:

* Michele Catasta, President and Head of AI, Replit * Karan Parekh, Head of Finance, Clay * Aisling O'Reilly, Director of Product Monetization, Fin * Ryan Campbell, Senior Director of Strategic Finance, Snowflake

Join us September 9–10 in Sonoma, California.

articles.title: WHAT PEOPLE *REALLY* THINK ABOUT IC WORK
articles.summary: Most tech workers want more IC work, but pay and influence keep many in management. High-impact IC roles could offer a better path by rewarding autonomy and business impact without requiring people management.

articles.title: NVIDIA'S RISKY BUSINESS
articles.summary: AI's infrastructure boom is relying on increasingly risky financing. Nvidia can keep the buildout going by attracting new pools of capital, but the strategy depends on AI revenues growing fast enough to justify the investment.

articles.title: WHAT THREE SECONDS OF MUSIC TAUGHT ME ABOUT PRODUCT
articles.summary: Strategic constraints sharpen product strategy by forcing teams to commit rather than endlessly iterating. Limiting choices preserves the core hypothesis, reduces decision fatigue, and empowers creative judgment without stifling critical thought.

articles.title: A GOOD MOVE IS CONSTRUCTIVE
articles.summary: Effective product strategy should emerge from consistently making good moves rather than from top-down planning. A constructive move strengthens an existing relationship or introduces useful structure, creates value on its own, and avoids relying on a hypothetical V2 or future follow-up to become worthwhile.

articles.title: INNOVATE AT SPEED WITH JIRA
articles.summary: Jira by Atlassian [11] is built for AI-native software development. The Teamwork Graph feeds agents context from across your entire stack, delivering 44% more accurate results. So you can equip every agent, team, and teammate in your org with the context they need to run faster in the same direction. Learn more [11].

articles.title: MONETIZING AI: A MODERN FRAMEWORK FOR HOW COMPANIES CAN MAXIMIZE BUSINESS GROWTH
articles.summary: AI is often expensive for vendors, who absorb high development costs without capturing equivalent value. A new framework suggests pricing based on measurable customer outcomes and AI usage, shifting from flat subscriptions to tiered, hybrid, or outcome-based models as billing capabilities evolve.

articles.title: TENSION-BASED PRIORITIZATION (A NON-FRAMEWORK)
articles.summary: Better prioritization starts by identifying the tensions preventing teams from acting on what they already know. Those recurring conflicts often reveal the real decisions more clearly than any framework.

articles.title: HOW TO STAY HAPPY: 4 SECRETS FROM HISTORY'S HAPPIEST PHILOSOPHER
articles.summary: Lasting happiness comes from replacing judgment with curiosity. Understand what drives your emotions and behavior, gain perspective, and use that insight to respond more calmly and make better choices.

articles.title: SHAPE UP FOR DATA TEAMS
articles.summary: Shape Up can work for Data teams only when they help shape priorities from the start. Without a seat at the betting table, they remain reactive service teams rather than true partners.

articles.title: PERFECTION IS NOT OVER-ENGINEERING
articles.summary: Over-engineering comes from solving the wrong problems.

articles.title: HOW TO WORK WITH DESIGNERS
articles.summary: Great design collaboration requires shared understanding, clear constraints, and iterative feedback.
